messages.en: Let's pick up where we left off at the coffee shop later, okay?
Sure, let me finish this work first.

senses.en_definition: To accept that something is true or exists.

collocations.en: believe that the news is true

senses.en_definition: To trust someone's character or ability; to feel confident that something can be achieved or will happen.

messages.en: I've got to give a presentation to the boss tomorrow. I'm worried I'll forget everything I've memorized.
I believe you can do it. You've practised loads of times, right? Just check your notes if you forget anything.

senses.en_definition: To trust someone or believe what they say (colloquial).
To entrust something to someone with full confidence that they will take care of it.

collocations.en: trust us to handle that matter

messages.en: Amir says he's already paid for the court booking, but I haven't seen a receipt yet.
I trust him, but just ask him for the receipt. It'll make it easier for us to check later.
Good point. I'll ask him now.

senses.en_definition: Used to urge someone to believe that something is true.
Used to urge someone to have confidence in a person's sincerity or ability, or in an outcome.

messages.en: The exam's tomorrow already. I'm scared I'll suddenly forget everything.
Trust me, you've done plenty of practice. You could even answer the hard questions yesterday.
You're right. I'll go over my notes a little more, then get some sleep.
